title: Web Search Chatbot
description: Health, latency, providers, cost, answer quality, documents, abuse, and usage. See docs/observability.md.

list.name: prompt_price
list.label: Model input $/1M tokens
list.description: Price per million prompt tokens for LLM_MODEL. Default: gpt-4o-mini.

list.name: completion_price
list.label: Model output $/1M tokens
list.description: Price per million completion tokens for LLM_MODEL. Default: gpt-4o-mini.

list.name: search_price
list.label: $ per web search
list.description: Default: one Tavily basic-search credit, pay as you go.

panels.title: API
panels.description: Whether Prometheus could scrape the API on its last attempt.

panels.title: Active streams
panels.description: Answers being streamed right now. Each is one open request that can last up to 90 s, so this, not requests per second, is the real concurrency.

panels.title: Run failure rate
panels.description: Failed runs as a share of all finished runs. A run is the whole product: this is the most important number on the board.

panels.title: Server error rate
panels.description: Responses with a 5xx status as a share of all responses.

panels.title: Time to first token (p95)
panels.description: How long the slowest 5% of users stare at an empty answer. Users feel this more than total answer time.

panels.title: DB pool in use
panels.description: Database connections checked out, as a share of the most the pool will open. At 100% requests queue for a connection: latency rises before errors do.

panels.title: Requests per second by status class
panels.description: All API responses. 4xx is often normal (an expired access token is a 401 before the client refreshes); a rise in 5xx is not.

panels.title: Latency p95 by route
panels.description: Time to response start. The run stream and the metrics scrape are left out: a stream's number is only its time to first byte. Click a legend entry to isolate a route.

panels.title: Server errors by route
panels.description: 5xx responses per minute, per route and status. Empty is good.

panels.title: Run outcomes per minute
panels.description: Every finished run: completed, failed, or cancelled. Cancellations are a proxy for frustration: people press Stop when an answer is slow or going the wrong way.

panels.title: Failures by error code (selected range)
panels.description: Why runs failed, by the stable code the client was shown. Codes are a closed set (run_timeout, llm_unavailable, run_interrupted, ...).

panels.title: Time to first token
panels.description: From run start to the first answer text. p50 is the typical user; p95 the unlucky one.

panels.title: Completed run duration
panels.description: Start to saved answer. The red line is the 90 s run deadline (RUN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS): a p95 creeping toward it means timeouts are next.

panels.title: Searches per run
panels.description: Web searches per finished run (the limit is MAX_SEARCHES_PER_RUN, default 3). Each search costs money and adds latency.

panels.title: Providers: is it us or them?
Provider failures per minute
panels.description: Failed calls to the language model, web search, and embeddings, by kind. Transient failures are retried; permanent ones (a bad key, a quota) need an operator.

panels.title: Search calls by outcome
panels.description: Calls to the search provider per minute.

panels.title: Search latency
panels.description: Per call. The red line is the 20 s per-search timeout.

panels.title: Embedding latency p95
panels.description: Embedding calls: whole documents at upload, and one question per document search.

panels.title: Cost, live (since the API last started)
Model tokens per minute
panels.description: Tokens the language model reported, by kind and model. Output tokens usually cost several times more than input tokens.

panels.title: Model tokens per completed run
panels.description: A prompt change or a looser search decision can double this without raising a single error. Only the trend shows it.

panels.title: Embedding tokens per minute
panels.description: Document ingestion and document-search questions.

panels.title: Unverified answers (selected range)
panels.description: Completed answers marked degraded: a search ran but no claim could be tied to a valid source, or the search failed. The user is told; this counts how often.

panels.title: What answers drew on
panels.description: Share of completed answers by the evidence the agent went for. A sudden shift means the search decision has changed behaviour (a new model, prompt, or heuristic).

panels.title: Document searches by outcome
panels.description: Searches of a conversation's PDFs: chunks found, nothing above the relevance floor (empty), or failed. Many empties mean the floor is too strict, or questions do not match the documents.

panels.title: Uploads by outcome (selected range)
panels.description: accepted, duplicate (same file already in the conversation), or the code the upload was refused with (pdf_invalid, pdf_no_text, pdf_too_large, ...).

panels.title: Ingestion results per minute
panels.description: Documents that finished background ingestion.

panels.title: Processing time p95
panels.description: Parsing a PDF (bounded at 30 s), and from a worker claiming it to ready.

panels.title: Stuck in processing
panels.description: Documents still processing ten minutes after their last update. Anything above zero usually means the ingestion worker died. From the database, so it survives restarts.

targets.rawSql: SELECT count(*) AS stuck FROM documents WHERE status = 'processing' AND updated_at < now() - interval '10 minutes'

panels.title: Rate-limit refusals per minute
panels.description: Requests refused with 429, by limit. One user hammering looks like a spike in one bucket; a broad rise may mean a limit is too tight.

panels.title: Auth refusals per minute
panels.description: 401 and 429 responses on /auth routes. A burst of failed logins is the classic sign of credential stuffing.

panels.title: Usage and spend (from the database: durable, daily)
Active users
panels.description: People who started at least one run in the selected range.

targets.rawSql: SELECT count(DISTINCT user_id) AS active FROM runs WHERE $__timeFilter(created_at)

panels.title: New sign-ups
panels.description: Accounts created in the selected range.

targets.rawSql: SELECT count(*) AS signups FROM users WHERE $__timeFilter(created_at)

panels.title: Runs
panels.description: Runs started in the selected range.

targets.rawSql: SELECT count(*) AS runs FROM runs WHERE $__timeFilter(created_at)

panels.title: Conversations started
panels.description: Conversations created in the selected range, deleted or not.

targets.rawSql: SELECT count(*) AS conversations FROM conversations WHERE $__timeFilter(created_at)

panels.title: Estimated spend (selected range)
panels.description: Tokens and searches recorded on runs and embedding usage, priced with the variables at the top of the dashboard. An estimate: check the providers' invoices.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT sum("Model input" + "Model output" + "Web search" + "Embeddings") AS spend FROM (
WITH model AS (
    SELECT date_trunc('day', created_at) AS day,
           sum(coalesce(prompt_tokens, 0)) AS prompt,
           sum(coalesce(completion_tokens, 0)) AS completion,
           sum(search_count) AS searches
    FROM runs WHERE $__timeFilter(created_at) GROUP BY 1
), embedding AS (
    SELECT date_trunc('day', created_at) AS day, sum(tokens) AS tokens
    FROM embedding_usage WHERE $__timeFilter(created_at) GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT coalesce(model.day, embedding.day) AS time,
       coalesce(model.prompt, 0) * ${prompt_price:sqlstring}::numeric / 1e6 AS "Model input",
       coalesce(model.completion, 0) * ${completion_price:sqlstring}::numeric / 1e6 AS "Model output",
       coalesce(model.searches, 0) * ${search_price:sqlstring}::numeric AS "Web search",
       coalesce(embedding.tokens, 0) * ${embedding_price:sqlstring}::numeric / 1e6 AS "Embeddings"
FROM model FULL JOIN embedding ON model.day = embedding.day
ORDER BY 1
) AS daily

panels.title: Daily active users
panels.description: Distinct users who started a run, per day.

targets.rawSql: SELECT date_trunc('day', created_at) AS time, count(DISTINCT user_id) AS "active users" FROM runs WHERE $__timeFilter(created_at) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Runs per day by status
panels.description: Runs started per day and how they ended.

targets.rawSql: SELECT date_trunc('day', created_at) AS time, status::text AS metric, count(*) AS runs FROM runs WHERE $__timeFilter(created_at) GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Estimated spend per day
panels.description: Same pricing as the total. Change the prices at the top of the dashboard when they change, or when you switch models.

targets.rawSql:
WITH model AS (
    SELECT date_trunc('day', created_at) AS day,
           sum(coalesce(prompt_tokens, 0)) AS prompt,
           sum(coalesce(completion_tokens, 0)) AS completion,
           sum(search_count) AS searches
    FROM runs WHERE $__timeFilter(created_at) GROUP BY 1
), embedding AS (
    SELECT date_trunc('day', created_at) AS day, sum(tokens) AS tokens
    FROM embedding_usage WHERE $__timeFilter(created_at) GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT coalesce(model.day, embedding.day) AS time,
       coalesce(model.prompt, 0) * ${prompt_price:sqlstring}::numeric / 1e6 AS "Model input",
       coalesce(model.completion, 0) * ${completion_price:sqlstring}::numeric / 1e6 AS "Model output",
       coalesce(model.searches, 0) * ${search_price:sqlstring}::numeric AS "Web search",
       coalesce(embedding.tokens, 0) * ${embedding_price:sqlstring}::numeric / 1e6 AS "Embeddings"
FROM model FULL JOIN embedding ON model.day = embedding.day
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: New sign-ups and conversations per day
panels.description: Growth: accounts created and conversations started, per day.

targets.rawSql: SELECT date_trunc('day', created_at) AS time, count(*) AS "sign-ups" FROM users WHERE $__timeFilter(created_at) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
SELECT date_trunc('day', created_at) AS time, count(*) AS conversations FROM conversations WHERE $__timeFilter(created_at) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Documents uploaded per day
panels.description: By where ingestion ended up.

targets.rawSql: SELECT date_trunc('day', created_at) AS time, status::text AS metric, count(*) AS documents FROM documents WHERE $__timeFilter(created_at) GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Top failure codes (selected range)
panels.description: Durable counterpart of the live failure panel: survives API restarts.

targets.rawSql: SELECT error_code AS "Error code", count(*) AS "Runs", max(created_at) AS "Last seen" FROM runs WHERE status = 'failed' AND $__timeFilter(created_at) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 10
